items.title: A tight Gaussian law is carried by a separable closed subspace
items.statement: A tight centered Borel Gaussian probability on any real Banach space is carried by a separable closed linear subspace E; as an E-valued law it remains tight and Gaussian, and its ambient support equals its support in E.
items.strategy: Choose compact sets with probabilities tending to one, take the closed rational span of their countable dense union, and use Hahn–Banach to extend continuous linear functionals from E to the ambient Banach space.

items.title: Supremum distance controls local log-Gaussian density distances
items.statement: For p_w=e^w/∫e^w dν and p_0=p_{w_0}, if both normalizers are finite and positive and r=‖w−w_0‖∞≤1, then h(p_w,p_0)≤e^r r, KL(P_0∥P_w)≤(e^{2r}/2)r², and E_0[log(p_w/p_0)²]≤4r².
items.strategy: Write g=w−w0 and c=log E0 e^g. Bound |c|≤r, apply the exponential Taylor remainder to the centered g for directional KL, and bound the normalized log-density ratio pointwise for Hellinger and its second moment.

items.title: The L² link norm controls binary-regression likelihood distances
items.statement: For q_w(x,y)=Ψ(w(x))^y(1−Ψ(w(x)))^{1−y} relative to G⊗counting measure, with G a probability and L=sup|Ψ′|, R=sup|Ψ′/[Ψ(1−Ψ)]| finite, d₂(q_w,q_{w0})²≤2L²‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}, KL(Q_0∥Q_w)≤LR‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}/2, and E_0[log(q_w/q_{w0})²]≤R²‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}.
items.strategy: Use the mean-value bound for Ψ, differentiate the Bernoulli directional KL in its second logit, and bound both Bernoulli log-probability derivatives by R.

items.title: Empirical mean and scale distance control Gaussian-regression likelihoods
items.statement: For independent Y_i∼N(w_0(x_i),σ_0²), model Y_i∼N(w(x_i),σ²), σ,σ0∈[a,b] with 0<a<b, and max_i|w(x_i)−w0(x_i)|≤1, |σ−σ0|≤1, the averages of KL(P_{i0}∥P_i) and E_0[log(p_i/p_{i0})²] are each bounded by C_{a,b}(‖w−w0‖_n²+|σ−σ0|²).
items.strategy: Compute the normal KL formula and expand the log likelihood ratio as a constant plus linear and centered quadratic functions of the true Gaussian error; bound the scale-only term by its vanishing first derivative at σ0.

items.title: Linear and quadratic Gaussian statistics have exponential tails
items.statement: For independent standard normals Z_i, fixed c_i, σ≤b, and Q=n^{-1}∑(δ_i+σZ_i)² with ‖δ‖_n≤1, the centered linear statistic n^{-1}∑c_iσZ_i has two-sided tail 2exp(−nt²/(2σ²‖c‖_n²)); for 0<t≤b²+2, P(|Q−(σ²+‖δ‖_n²)|≥t)≤2exp(−nt²/(4V_b)), V_b=2b⁴+4b².
items.strategy: Complete the square to compute the scalar Gaussian moment generating function and the noncentral squared-normal moment generating function; bound the latter near zero and optimize the exponential-Markov inequality.

items.title: Local KL and log-square mass bounds a non-IID posterior denominator
items.statement: For independent dominated observations and a prior subset of mass at least e^{−Cnε²} on which average directional KL and average log-likelihood second moment are each at most ε², the full likelihood-ratio denominator is finite almost surely and is at least e^{−(C+2)nε²} with probability at least 1−1/(nε²).
items.strategy: Bound the integrated likelihood ratio in expectation using independence and Tonelli; Jensen lower-bounds the denominator by the prior-averaged log likelihood, whose mean and variance are bounded by nε², and Chebyshev gives the stated event.

items.title: Tests and a sieve tail imply posterior contraction from a denominator bound
items.statement: If a dominated full-data likelihood denominator is at least e^{−A nε²} with probability tending to one, the prior mass outside a measurable sieve is at most e^{−B nε²} with B>A, and a test has null and uniform sieve type-II errors at most e^{−T nε²} with T>A, then posterior mass outside the tested set tends to zero in P0 probability.
items.strategy: Split the likelihood numerator into tested sieve mass and sieve tail, change measure to bound their expectations, and apply Markov after dividing by the denominator lower bound.

items.title: Supremum sieves admit tests in fixed-design Gaussian regression
items.statement: For fixed design, σ∈[a,b], ε_n→0, nε_n²→∞ and a measurable sieve B_n with log N(3ε_n,B_n,‖·‖∞)≤6C nε_n², for any T>0 a sufficiently large fixed M gives tests of H0:(w0,σ0) against (w,σ)∈B_n×[a,b] with ‖w−w0‖_n+|σ−σ0|>Mε_n whose null and uniform alternative errors are at most e^{−Tnε_n²}.
items.strategy: Cover the mean functions; use Gaussian linear-score tests when the empirical mean distance is large and upper/lower residual-energy tests when the scale distance is large; union-bound the finite cover and use the Gaussian quadratic tail bound.

items.title: A nonzero Gaussian prior forces logarithmic small-ball cost
items.statement: If a continuous linear functional ℓ has Var(ℓ(W))>0, then for sufficiently small ε the concentration function satisfies φ_{w0}(ε)≥log(1/ε)−C_ℓ for every w0, because the centered Gaussian small-ball probability is at most a constant times ε and the RKHS approximation cost is nonnegative.
items.strategy: The norm ball {‖W‖<ε} is contained in {|ℓ(W)|<‖ℓ‖ε}; bound the latter by the maximum density of its nondegenerate scalar Gaussian law and use the nonnegative RKHS cost.

items.title: Gaussian-process posterior contraction in density and regression models
items.statement: Under ε_n→0, nε_n²→∞ and the stated Banach Gaussian concentration condition, the draft treats log-Gaussian density estimation in Hellinger distance, binary regression in L²(G), and fixed-design Gaussian regression in empirical L² plus scale distance; the last branch still has an unresolved scale-local-mass case.
items.strategy: Use the exact half-squared RKHS concentration convention and its support/sieve interfaces; prove model-specific likelihood-distance bounds; apply IID entropy tests and denominator bounds in the first two branches, and direct Gaussian score/energy tests with a non-IID denominator in fixed design. The fixed-scale local-mass gap remains escalated.

items.title: Small L² log-density perturbations can remain far in Hellinger distance
items.statement: On [0,1] with Lebesgue measure, w_k=k 1_[0,k^{-4}] tends to zero in L² while the normalized log-density p_k=e^{w_k}/∫e^{w_k} remains at Hellinger distance tending to √2 from the uniform truth.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the L² norm, normalizer and Hellinger affinity explicitly; the normalized prior density concentrates on the shrinking spike.

items.title: A degenerate GP concentration function does not control unknown-scale prior mass
items.statement: For W≡0 and w0=0 the half-squared-RKHS concentration function is zero; ε_n=√(log log n/n) satisfies φ(ε_n)≤nε_n² and nε_n²→∞, while a uniform scale prior has negative log local mass asymptotic to (1/2)log n, not O(nε_n²). This identifies a missing denominator-mass check, not a posterior counterexample.
items.strategy: Verification: the prior is a point mass on the zero function, so its RKHS approximation and centered small-ball costs vanish; calculate the interval mass and compare log n with log log n.

items.title: A constant Gaussian log-density prior gives the uniform density exactly
items.statement: On the unit interval, W(x)=Z for Z∼N(0,1) induces the uniform density for every prior draw; for w0=0 and ε_n=√(log n/n), the concentration condition holds and the density posterior is exactly at truth.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the normalizer, RKHS approximation term and scalar Gaussian small-ball lower bound; then normalize the identical likelihoods.

items.title: A one-point logistic GP regression satisfies the L² link branch
items.statement: For a one-point covariate space, G=δ_x and W(x)=Z∼N(0,1), the logistic link has bounded derivative and bounded derivative-to-Bernoulli-variance ratio, w0=0 is in support, and ε_n=√(log n/n) satisfies the GP concentration inequality.
items.strategy: Verification: evaluate the link constants, concentration function and L²(G) identification, then instantiate the binary-regression branch.

items.title: A constant GP on a repeated fixed design meets the nondegenerate scale branch
items.statement: For repeated design point x0, W(x)=Z∼N(0,1), w0=0, σ0=1 and an independent uniform prior σ∼Unif[1/2,3/2], ε_n=2√(log n/n) satisfies the concentration and scale-local-mass conditions for empirical-L²-plus-scale contraction.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the scalar GP concentration bound, the uniform scale interval mass, and verify the fixed design and compact scale hypotheses.
